notes.contender: Five Andorran titles (incl. 2025, 2026) and three cups since 2020; first Andorran club in a European league phase.
notes.stewardship: Private club, backed early by builder Construccions Modernes; chairman Pablo Gomez (estimate).
notes.city: Club of Escaldes-Engordany in Andorra, where football draws very small crowds.

notes.contender: 5th in 2024-25 and 2025-26, cup finals 2018 and 2026; 3rd in 2018 and 2021; last trophy 2013.
notes.stewardship: Businessman Jakub Střeštík bought the majority from Miroslav Pelta, jailed for subsidy fraud, who kept a role in the club.
notes.voice: Privately owned company; no fan influence found.
notes.city: Main club of Jablonec nad Nisou (~45,000); limited pull (estimate).

notes.stewardship: Sam Baro, about 95-97% since 2023 (EUR 30m), conventional private owner
notes.city: Ghent's main club, strong local following

notes.contender: Kazakh champions 2020, 2024, 2025; cups 2015-2021; first UCL league phase 2025-26
notes.stewardship: Private owner Kairat Boranbayev (arrested 2022); city council holds a 30% minority stake since 2015 and funds the club
notes.voice: No documented fan role in ownership or decisions
notes.city: Almaty's main club, nicknamed 'The Nation's Team'

notes.contender: First Lithuanian title 2025; LFF Cup 2026; regular top three since 2020.
notes.stewardship: Local owners: Paulius Motiejunas (70%) and basketball great Mantas Kalnietis (30%, chairman).
notes.voice: Privately owned; no supporter role found.
notes.city: Kaunas's main football club, but the city lives through basketball (Zalgiris BC).

notes.contender: Veikkausliiga champions 2019, 2024, 2025; cups 2021, 2022, 2024; Conference League knockout round 2025-26.
notes.stewardship: Main owner Ari Lahti (Finnish investor, FA president), funding the club about a million euros a year since the 2000s.
notes.voice: KuPS ry (members' association) holds the league place and leases it to the company; some structure, little documented fan power.
notes.city: Kuopio's football club; the city also follows KalPa hockey.

notes.contender: 30 Gibraltar titles incl. six straight (2021-2026); Rock Cup 2026.
notes.stewardship: Run by a club board under president Dylan Viagas; no outside investor reported (estimate).
notes.voice: No documented supporter ownership or influence (estimate).
notes.city: Gibraltar's dominant club, but a small territory where football is a minor pastime.

notes.contender: First Allsvenskan title 2025 and Svenska Cupen 2025-26; before that a mid-table club.
notes.stewardship: Member-owned non-profit association; chairman Jan Sjöblom.
notes.voice: Swedish member association under the 51% rule; members elect the board.
notes.city: The pride of Hälleviks fishing village (about 800 people) and Sölvesborg; 2025 title squad mostly local-born.

notes.contender: Cypriot champions 2025, cups 2024 and 2026; Champions League league phase 2025-26.
notes.stewardship: Russian billionaire Sergey Lomakin (Fix Price) with chairman Roman Dubov via Total Sports Investments; part of a loose network with Riga FC.
notes.city: Paphos's main club, but a 2014 merger with shallow roots.

notes.stewardship: Giannis Alafouzos (Skai TV owner), private, long-term
notes.voice: Briefly fan-owned via Panathinaikos Alliance (2012); now owner-run
notes.city: One of Greece's most supported clubs; shares Athens with AEK and Olympiacos

notes.contender: Ten Serbian titles 2016-2026, six straight doubles, UCL group stages
notes.stewardship: Run by the Crvena zvezda sports association, long reliant on political patrons and Gazprom sponsorship
notes.voice: Part of the Crvena zvezda sports society; no fan ownership, politically connected boards
notes.city: Serbia's most supported club but shares Belgrade with Partizan

notes.stewardship: Linked to Russian billionaire Sergey Lomakin (Fix Price), who also backs Pafos; ownership opaque, chairman Aleksandrs Pronins.
notes.voice: Privately controlled company (SIA); no supporter role.
notes.city: A 2015 creation in a city with several clubs and little football following.

notes.contender: Eliteserien runners-up 2016, 2023, 2024, 4th 2025; cup 2022, final 2026; first Europa League league phase 2025.
notes.stewardship: Member club with an elected board (chair Arild Mjøs Andersen); no outside owner.
notes.voice: Member association (Norwegian clubs must be member-controlled); members forced an extraordinary general meeting in 2021.
notes.city: Bergen's club, 'Bergens Stolthet'; the city's big team with strong public interest.

notes.contender: 3rd in the 2025-26 Pro League; mostly mid-to-low table before; no major honours.
notes.stewardship: DMM.com (Japanese company) since 2017; run largely as a European stepping stone for Japanese players.
notes.voice: Corporate owner; no fan influence found.
notes.city: The town's club since 1924; main identity of a small Limburg town (estimate).

notes.contender: Super Lig champions 2021-22 (7 titles), Turkish Cup 2025-26 (10 total); 3rd in 2023-24 and 2025-26.
notes.stewardship: Member club run by elected president Ertugrul Dogan; heavy debt and a 2019-20 UEFA FFP European ban.
notes.voice: Members' association: congress elects the president (Ertugrul Dogan, re-elected unopposed Nov 2024); the listed football company is controlled by the association.
notes.city: Trabzon's only major club and regional identity; first Anatolian club to break the Istanbul clubs' hold on the title.
